verdict.rationale: Gitea's automations are Gitea Actions workflows written as YAML in a GitHub Actions-compatible format. Gitea also natively provides commit history and Pull Request/AGit code review, so workflow definitions can be versioned and reviewed like any other code. However, the evidence never states that workflow files live in the repository and are governed by these features, and rollback is not documented anywhere. missing for 10: explicit documentation that workflow definitions are repo-stored and versioned, documented rollback/revert of automations, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Users can write workflows in familiar YAML format and reuse a variety of existing Actions plugins.
browsing commit history and code files, reviewing and merging code submissions
Code review supports both the Pull Request workflow and AGit workflow.
